248:     pub(crate) fn split_configured_words(
249:         &mut self,
250:         text: &NativeIntStr,
251:         debug_args: Option<&Vec<OsString>>,
252:     ) -> Result<Vec<NativeIntString>, parse_error::ParseError> {
253:         if self.do_input_debug_printing == Some(true) || debug_args.is_some() {

260:         let input_is_empty = iterator.expander.parser.input.is_empty();
261:         let pointer = iterator.expander.parser.pointer;
262:         let remaining_is_empty = iterator.expander.parser.remaining.is_empty();
263:         let peek_end = match iterator.expander.parser.peek() {
264:             Err(parse_err) => parse_err.peek_position >= iterator.expander.parser.input.len(),
265:             Ok(_) => remaining_is_empty && pointer >= iterator.expander.parser.input.len(),
266:         };
267:         let output_is_empty = iterator.expander.output.is_empty();
268:         let words_is_empty = iterator.words.is_empty();
269:         if input_is_empty && output_is_empty && words_is_empty && peek_end {
270:             if !self.had_string_argument {
271:                 self.had_string_argument = true;
272:             }
273:             return Ok(iterator.words);
274:         }
275: 
276:         iterator.state_root()?;
277:         if !self.had_string_argument {
278:             self.had_string_argument = true;
279:         }
280:         Ok(iterator.words)

420:     fn run_program(
421:         &mut self,
422:         opts: &Options<'_>,
423:         do_debug_printing: bool,
424:     ) -> Result<(), Box<dyn UError>> {
425:         let prog = Cow::from(opts.program[0]);
426:         #[cfg(unix)]
427:         let mut arg0 = prog.clone();
428:         #[cfg(not(unix))]
429:         let arg0 = prog.clone();
430:         let args = &opts.program[1..];
431: 
432:         /*
433:          * On Unix-like systems Command::status either ends up calling either fork or posix_spawnp
434:          * (which ends up calling clone). Keep using the current process would be ideal, but the
435:          * standard library contains many checks and fail-safes to ensure the process ends up being
436:          * created. This is much simpler than dealing with the hassles of calling execvp directly.
437:          */
438:         let mut cmd = process::Command::new(&*prog);
439:         cmd.args(args);
440: 
441:         if let Some(_argv0) = opts.argv0 {
442:             #[cfg(unix)]
443:             {
444:                 cmd.arg0(_argv0);
445:                 arg0 = Cow::Borrowed(_argv0);
446:                 if do_debug_printing {
447:                     eprintln!("argv0:     {}", arg0.quote());
448:                 }
449:             }
450: 
451:             #[cfg(not(unix))]
452:             return Err(USimpleError::new(
453:                 2,
454:                 "--argv0 is currently not supported on this platform",
455:             ));
456:         }
457: 
458:         if do_debug_printing {
459:             eprintln!("executing: {}", prog.maybe_quote());
460:             let arg_prefix = "   arg";
461:             eprintln!("{}[{}]= {}", arg_prefix, 0, arg0.quote());
462:             for (i, arg) in args.iter().enumerate() {
463:                 eprintln!("{}[{}]= {}", arg_prefix, i + 1, arg.quote());
464:             }
465:         }
466: 
467:         match cmd.status() {
468:             Ok(exit) if !exit.success() => {
469:                 #[cfg(unix)]
470:                 if let Some(exit_code) = exit.code() {
471:                     return Err(exit_code.into());
472:                 } else {
473:                     // `exit.code()` returns `None` on Unix when the process is terminated by a signal.
474:                     // See std::os::unix::process::ExitStatusExt for more information. This prints out
475:                     // the interrupted process and the signal it received.
476:                     let signal_code = exit.signal().unwrap();
477:                     let signal = Signal::try_from(signal_code).unwrap();
478: 
479:                     // We have to disable any handler that's installed by default.
480:                     // This ensures that we exit on this signal.
481:                     // For example, `SIGSEGV` and `SIGBUS` have default handlers installed in Rust.
482:                     // We ignore the errors because there is not much we can do if that fails anyway.
483:                     // SAFETY: The function is unsafe because installing functions is unsafe, but we are
484:                     // just defaulting to default behavior and not installing a function. Hence, the call
485:                     // is safe.
486:                     let _ = unsafe {
487:                         sigaction(
488:                             signal,
489:                             &SigAction::new(SigHandler::SigDfl, SaFlags::empty(), SigSet::all()),
490:                         )
491:                     };
492: 
493:                     let _ = raise(signal);
494:                 }
495:                 return Err(exit.code().unwrap().into());
496:             }
497:             Err(ref err)
498:                 if (err.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound)
499:                     || (err.kind() == io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput) =>
500:             {
501:                 return Err(self.make_error_no_such_file_or_dir(prog.deref()));
502:             }
503:             Err(e) => {
504:                 uucore::show_error!("unknown error: {:?}", e);
505:                 return Err(126.into());
506:             }
507:             Ok(_) => (),
508:         }
509:         Ok(())
510:     }
511: }
